title: fix(release): the post-publish npm check races the registry and only ever looks at 1 of 69 packages — it red-flagged a release that had fully succeeded
body:
Found on the **17.3.0 release**: Release run `8330`, job `100996109699` ([log](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/33864464755/job/100996109699)). The release **succeeded completely** — all 69 packages plus `create-objectstack` are on npm, verified one by one — and the job still exited 1.

## The failing step

`.github/workflows/release.yml`, the last thing the `publish` job does:

```bash
pnpm run release

# `changeset publish` skips versions already on the registry, so a
# re-dispatch over a partially-published release is a repair, not a
# duplicate. What is NOT optional is that the version is on npm when
# this step ends.
if ! npm view "@objectstack/cli@$VERSION" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "::error::publish ran but @objectstack/cli@$VERSION is still not on npm"
  exit 1
fi
echo "published=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

## What actually happened, measured from npm's own `time` field

`@objectstack/cli@17.3.0` was committed by npm at **10:53:25.108Z**. The check ran at **10:53:32** — **seven seconds later** — and reported it absent. npm's write path and its CDN-fronted read path are eventually consistent; seven seconds is well inside that window.

The wider fact the fix has to be designed against: **npm took ~8 minutes to commit the 69-package burst**, and `changeset publish` had already printed `Successfully published` for all of them at 10:53:25.

| package | npm `time[17.3.0]` |
|:--|:--|
| `console` / `spec` / `types` / `core` | 10:52:39 – 10:52:55 |
| `account` / `studio` / `client` / `metadata` / `plugin-security` / `rest` | 10:53:00 – 10:53:13 |
| **`cli`** | **10:53:25.108** ← the check fired at 10:53:32 |
| `objectql` / `setup` / `service-storage` / `hono` | 10:55:23 – 10:55:58 |
| `formula` | 10:57:06 |
| `verify` | 10:59:31 |
| `runtime` | **11:00:32** |

So `Successfully published` is changesets' belief (the npm CLI returned success); `time[version]` is when the registry committed. Under a 69-package burst from one account those diverge by minutes.

## Two defects

**① No retry.** One shot, immediately after a burst publish. Every release is a bet on how fast npm's read path settles. This is the direct cause of the false red.

**② It checks 1 package of 69.** The one thing it verifies is `@objectstack/cli`. Had a package genuinely failed to publish, this step would not have seen it — and the false red on `cli` would have *masked* it. That is the more expensive defect: it is the case the step exists for, and the case it cannot detect. Concretely, `@objectstack/runtime` was the last to commit at 11:00:32; between 10:53 and 11:00 the fixed group really was partially readable, and nothing in this step was looking.

## Acceptance

- **Retry with bounded backoff** before concluding absence. Absence after the budget is still a hard failure — ⛔ the step must keep failing CLOSED. No `|| true`, no dropping the `exit 1`, no downgrade to a warning.
- **Verify every package the publish reports**, not just `@objectstack/cli` — derived from the publish output or the workspace's published-package set, ⛔ never a hand-transcribed list (this repo has 69 and the count moves).
- **Name what is missing.** On failure the error must say *which* packages are absent, so the repair dispatch (`workflow_dispatch` with `force`) has something to act on. The current message names a package that was fine.
- **Reproduce, then show green.** The regression is reproducible without npm: a version that exists but whose read is cold. Show the old shape failing and the new one absorbing it.
- If the logic moves into `scripts/`, it carries a **self-test** with a registered case floor, per the #13799 recipe now in wide use — a verifier whose own cases can silently stop running is the same class of bug as the one being fixed.

## ⛔ Out of scope, and load-bearing

- **Do not touch the publish gating.** `environment: release` (Required reviewers, ADR-0125 D3), the `publish-pending` predicate, `force`'s dispatch-only semantics, and the `success() && (...)` parenthesisation are the "ONLY A HUMAN PUBLISHES" invariant (maintainer ruling, quoted verbatim at the top of the file after the rc.3 / rc.4 incident). This card touches the **verification after** publish, nothing about **whether** publish runs.
- **Do not touch `release-integrity`.** Its `published` output is `image-missing` and it mints nothing; it is not part of this defect. (It is, however, why the GitHub Releases appeared at 11:00:23 — the no-mint backfill, working as designed.)
- ⛔ **No auto-merge will be armed on this PR.** `release.yml` is the one file in the repository that publishes; a human reviews it whatever the Governed Surface Guard says about the path.

## Not a defect, recorded so it is not re-investigated

The 17.3.0 release itself is **complete and correct**. All 69 packages + `create-objectstack` were checked individually against `registry.npmjs.org` and every one answers 200 for 17.3.0. There was exactly **one** publish, from the run the maintainer approved; the later Release runs (`8331`, `8332`) were push-triggered by ordinary merge-queue landings and their `publish` jobs were **skipped**, because by then `cli@17.3.0` was on npm and `publish-pending` was false. No second publisher existed.
